business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Tempsens designs and manufactures customised temperature sensing solutions, electrical heating solutions and specialised cables for industrial process applications. Products are made-to-order for end users in metals, petrochemicals, power, defence and nuclear, glass, plastics and manufacturing, sold both as high-barrier Project/OEM supply (67.55% of Fiscal 2026 revenue from operations excluding other operating revenue) and as recurring MRO replacement business (32.45%). It served more than 1,000 unique customers between April 1, 2023 and March 31, 2026 and exported to more than 80 countries over the same period.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Heavily backward-integrated manufacture. 'We are among the very few companies in the world with a backward-integrated manufacturing facility for thermocouples, cables, and electrical heaters, located at Udaipur, India, as of March 31, 2026 (Source: F&S Report).' Key in-house capabilities now include alloy melting, hot-rolling, annealing, mineral-insulated cable manufacturing, machining, final assembly and calibration: 'Previously, we relied on external suppliers for most metallurgical finished goods, but by internalising these critical steps, we have reduced our dependence on third parties.' For heater products the Company manufactures heating alloys, produces tubular heating elements, fabricates vessels and performs final assembly including instrumentation, process connections and panel integration entirely in-house, and also produces the thermocouple conductor used in thermocouple cables - stated to have 'increased operational control, enhanced product consistency, and allowed us to shorten lead times'. Certain units manufacture products used as raw materials by other units as well as being supplied to external customers. New products are frequently used internally before external launch (thermowells, thermocouple cables, mineral-insulated and specialised cables, thermocouple and heating-alloy nickel-based conductors). Indigenisation is framed under 'Make in India': thermocouple and heating conductors previously imported are now manufactured in-house, and the Company states it has 'reduced reliance on foreign suppliers' by indigenising non-contact temperature sensor development. Manufacturing is make-to-order: 'Each manufacturing job operates on a make-to-order basis, i.e., customer requirements are translated into detailed engineering and design workflows, resulting in precise production drawings.' INPUTS: metals and alloys (platinum, nickel, stainless steel, copper, inconel), insulating materials (magnesium oxide, ceramics, fibreglass, PTFE), coatings (silicone, PVC, polyimide). Cost of materials procured from India was Rs 2,095.61 / 1,681.12 / 1,419.40 million and from outside India Rs 512.04 / 408.29 / 235.76 million for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024, i.e. 80.36% / 80.46% / 85.76% domestic and 19.64% / 19.54% / 14.24% imported; purchases during the year were Rs 2,607.65 / 2,089.41 / 1,655.16 million (71.63% / 69.12% / 72.88% of total expenses) and cost of materials consumed Rs 2,484.25 / 1,985.13 / 1,717.06 million (68.24% / 65.67% / 75.60% of total expenses). Suppliers span 18 Indian states and two union territories and 18 foreign countries (including China, USA, UK, Singapore, Germany, Israel, France, Austria, Czech Republic, Japan, South Korea, Indonesia, UAE, Thailand, Canada, Taiwan and Hong Kong). FORWARD/OUTBOUND: no owned logistics - 'We rely on third-party logistics providers ... We do not operate our own logistics fleet, nor do we conduct logistics operations through related party transactions. We rely on spot-based arrangements with third-party logistics providers, utilising air, road, and rail transportation modes.' R&D is conducted entirely in-house with a dedicated team of 83 employees as of March 31, 2026 (10.20% of total group headcount of 814); granted IP comprises 12 patents in India, eight registered trademarks in India, one copyright registration in India and 39 trademark registrations outside India, with one patent, four Indian trademarks and three foreign trademarks pending. Working capital: Net Working Capital Days of 210 / 193 / 152 for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024 (days sales outstanding plus days inventory outstanding minus days payable outstanding), the increase 'primarily attributable to a higher inventory holding resulting from customization requirements, delays in dispatch clearance, and the impact of the amalgamation of Marathon Heater ... acquisition of Tempsens GmbH, Tempsens Polaska and Tempsens Measurement and Control Private Limited'.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue from operations grew 17.53% to ₹4,448.78 million in Fiscal 2026, led by electrical heating solutions (+44.89%) on major order execution and deeper penetration in industrial and renewables segments, with temperature sensing +12.73% and specialised cables +11.06%
- Mix shift toward electrical heating, which was 20.70% of Fiscal 2026 vertical revenue versus 3.90% in Fiscal 2024, following the Marathon Heater amalgamation and operationalisation of Unit VI
- Export-led growth - revenue from outside India rose to ₹1,258.21 million (28.52% of revenue excluding other operating revenue) in Fiscal 2026 from ₹586.36 million (21.49%) in Fiscal 2024, a stated 46.49% CAGR between Fiscals 2024 and 2026
- Working capital cycle lengthening - Net Working Capital Days rose to 210 in Fiscal 2026 from 193 in Fiscal 2025 and 152 in Fiscal 2024, primarily on higher inventory holding from customisation requirements, dispatch clearance delays and the Marathon Heater amalgamation
- Input cost and volume effect - cost of material consumed rose 25.14% to ₹2,484.25 million on higher production volumes and higher commodity input costs, against a 17.53% revenue increase; total expenses rose 20.42% to ₹3,640.39 million
- Inventory build of ₹83.27 million credited to the statement of profit and loss in Fiscal 2026 as stock was raised to support anticipated demand after capacity expansions
- Other income rose 178.46% to ₹109.77 million on interest income from higher fixed deposit balances (₹47.98 million) and net foreign exchange gains (₹34.83 million)
- Contract liabilities (customer advances) increased to ₹119.94 million as at March 31, 2026 from ₹70.42 million a year earlier, which management describes as indicating a growing order book
- Reported profitability is not comparable across years - Fiscal 2026 reflects the GmbH, Polska and Tempsens Measurement acquisitions and Fiscal 2025 the Marathon Heater amalgamation, so the Company also presents Adjusted PAT and Adjusted ROE excluding Ind AS 103 intangible amortisation and goodwill (Adjusted ROE 20.70% versus reported ROE 13.54% in Fiscal 2026)
- R&D expense stepped up to ₹11.62 million in Fiscal 2026 from ₹5.07 million in Fiscal 2025

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Expand and commercialise new products by leveraging R&D capabilities and technological partnerships - developing specialised thermocouples, mid-voltage heaters and a new line of high-precision infrared pyrometers and online thermal imagers
- Prioritise solutions for emerging industries - battery energy storage systems, decarbonisation, fuel cells, green hydrogen, advanced exhaust heating for automotive emission control, defence and aerospace, metal recycling and nuclear power
- Scale established product lines - process heating, nickel alloy conductor solutions and infrared technology - by expanding production capacity, automating key manufacturing processes and strengthening global distribution and after-sales engineering support
- Maintain and expand global presence and export sales - enter Europe, the Middle East, North America and South America, register with major end users, EPC companies and OEMs, and invest in international certifications for products and facilities
- Continue growth through organic and inorganic initiatives, including mergers, acquisitions, alliances, new joint ventures and subsidiaries, pursuing consolidation of fragmented target markets at attractive valuations
- Continue to focus on improving operational efficiency and expanding manufacturing capacity - process optimisation, automation and digital systems, energy-efficient practices, proposed expansion of Unit VI, and additional land procured for future expansion
- Deepen backward integration to control critical inputs, optimise raw material utilisation and reduce reliance on external suppliers
- Expand the replacement (MRO) business and diversify industry presence across metals, petrochemicals, defence and nuclear, manufacturing, power, trading, glass and plastics to drive resilient, annuity-style growth

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Growth is pursued on three fronts. First, brownfield capacity at Udaipur: the Net Proceeds fund plant, machinery and equipment for the electrical heating solutions vertical at Unit VI and the specialised cable solutions vertical at Unit IV, plus civil and building work for sheds and related infrastructure on existing vacant land within the Unit VI premises, so the machinery goes into existing sites rather than a new location. Following the proposed capital expenditure, electrical heating installed capacity rises from 317,400 units to 341,400 units (+7.56%) and specialised cable capacity from 10,200 kilometres to 11,400 kilometres (+11.76%), with nickel alloy conductor capacity unchanged at 400 metric tons; management has also procured additional land on which further expansion may be envisaged. Second, inorganic and partnership-led expansion: the Marathon Heater amalgamation (effective March 6, 2025, appointed date April 1, 2024), the acquisitions of Tempsens Instruments GmbH and Tempsens Polska (effective January 16, 2026) and of Tempsens Measurement and Control (March 30, 2026), plus technology joint ventures such as Pyrosens with Micro-Epsilon and Victura Tempsens for automotive cables. Third, geographic expansion: 15 manufacturing units worldwide including Joint Ventures (ten in Udaipur, five overseas in the UAE, South Korea, Indonesia, Germany and Poland), a sales presence being established in Mexico where the entity is registered but capital infusion is still ongoing, and a stated push into Europe, the Middle East, North America and South America backed by continued investment in international product and facility certifications.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Largest manufacturer of contact and non-contact temperature sensors in India by revenue as of March 31, 2026 with approximately 10.5% temperature-sensor market share in Fiscal 2026, and the only Indian manufacturer of non-contact temperature sensors with approximately 21.3% share (Source: F&S Report - commissioned industry report, not the issuer's own market data)
- Only manufacturer in India of fibre optic temperature sensors and thermal profiling systems as of March 31, 2026 and of pyrometers and online thermal imagers in Fiscal 2026; among the very few specialist makers of advanced conductor solutions (Source: F&S Report)
- Diversified business model with three verticals, wide industry coverage and a balanced mix of Project/OEM (67.55% of Fiscal 2026 revenue excluding other operating revenue) and recurring MRO revenue (32.45%)
- Make-to-order engineering with approval-driven entry barriers - extended qualification periods, in-depth testing and field trials before supplier approval, supporting customer retention and cross-selling
- Established R&D capabilities - 83 dedicated R&D employees as at March 31, 2026; 12 patents granted in India, eight registered trademarks in India, one copyright registration and 39 trademark registrations outside India
- Global presence through subsidiaries and joint ventures in India, UAE, Germany, Poland, Indonesia and South Korea, exports to more than 80 countries between April 1, 2023 and March 31, 2026, and 28 distributors as of March 31, 2026
- Integrated global operations with backward integration from alloy melting to final calibration, digital batch/lot traceability and a three-gate inspection regime
- Low customer concentration - top 10 customers contributed 18.59%, 23.68% and 24.74% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, consistently at or under 25.00%
- Operations led by the Promoters and supported by an experienced management team; 814 permanent employees together with the Joint Ventures as of March 31, 2026

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Dependence on Projects/OEM business — Projects/OEM contributed 67.55%, 69.16% and 63.99% of revenue from operations (excluding scrap sale and export incentive) in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. These are large, sometimes one-time orders with long sales cycles whose timing and volume move with customer capital expenditure cycles.
- End-user industry concentration in metals and petrochemicals — Metal and petrochemical industries collectively contributed 41.13%, 42.90% and 41.52% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; a downturn in these cyclical sectors would directly reduce demand.
- Working capital intensity — Net Working Capital Days rose to 210 in Fiscal 2026 from 193 in Fiscal 2025 and 152 in Fiscal 2024 on higher inventory from customisation and dispatch clearance delays, tying up cash and increasing reliance on borrowings as the business scales.
- Raw material price volatility and import dependence — Inputs include copper, aluminium, stainless steel, nickel alloys, platinum and rhodium; ₹512.04 million or 19.64% of Fiscal 2026 purchases were sourced outside India, exposing costs to commodity prices, logistics, tariffs and currency movements.
- Acquisition-driven growth and non-comparable financials — Fiscal 2026 reflects the Tempsens GmbH, Tempsens Polska and Tempsens Measurement acquisitions and Fiscal 2025 the Marathon Heater amalgamation, which created goodwill of ₹1,061.28 million; management states the years are not directly comparable and reported ROE is depressed by the resulting goodwill and intangibles.
- Joint venture and overseas subsidiary control limitations — Key actions in the joint ventures require majority, unanimous or partner consent, and in the JVs and the overseas subsidiary the chief executive or a board member is often a shareholder or a shareholder's relative, complicating incentives and enforcement; control of Tempsens Instruments GmbH rests on a governance agreement over a 50.00% stake.
- Export and international expansion exposure — Revenue from outside India was 28.52%, 26.70% and 21.49% of revenue (excluding other operating revenue) in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, exposing the business to currency movements, trade restrictions and local regulation, and to the risk that new markets such as Mexico do not scale.
- Low utilisation of newly added capacity — Electrical heating installed capacity jumped to 317,400 units in Fiscal 2025 from 2,200 in Fiscal 2024, yet vertical utilisation was 54.75% in Fiscal 2026 (Unit VI at 41.35%) and conductor capacity ran at 55.75%, so further capex must be absorbed before it earns a return.
